extracted.intended_audience: marketing and PR professionals, brand managers, communications students, and agency creatives
extracted.subtask_description: A case-study style analysis of an advertising-driven PR crisis (Pepsi/Kendall Jenner) highlighting failures in research, casting, creative process, and crisis response, intended to derive lessons for brand and communications practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Market research and vetting
rubrics_metrics.description: One main issue critics had with PepsiCo and the “Jump In” spot was the lack of market research so clearly depicted in the final video.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct thorough market research and reach out to consumers before rollout; bring in outside perspectives or agencies to vet creative. The page cites Marketing Week: marketers need an outside perspective, whether from an ad agency or by conducting thorough market research and reaching out to consumers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity in decision-making
rubrics_metrics.description: The ad failure shows the importance of diversity and market research: 'The Kendall Jenner Pepsi fiasco is a perfect example of what happens when there’s no black people in the room when decisions are being made.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure diverse representation among creators and approvers so tone and cultural implications are caught. The page references a One Poll survey finding nearly half of marketers believe brands fail to reflect modern, racially diverse humanity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate spokesperson/casting relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Although it is obviously considered a coup to recruit a famous face, it must be an appropriate, relevant person in relation to the core significance of the specific campaign — Jenner is not known for activism or speaking out on social issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select spokespeople whose public persona and credentials align with the campaign’s subject matter; casting a celebrity without relevant authenticity risks perceived opportunism and backlash.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid co-opting social movements for commercial gain
rubrics_metrics.description: Critics condemned the ad for 'co-opting protest movements – such as Black Lives Matter – for commercial gain' and for 'trivializing real-life protests.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use imagery, themes, or symbols of real social/political movements as marketing devices without genuine connection, consultation, or contribution; risk includes significant public condemnation and comparisons to real-life suffering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone sensitivity and context awareness
rubrics_metrics.description: Many things made people uncomfortable; some compared the ad to real protest images (e.g., Ieshia Evans), and viewers compared Jenner’s Pepsi offering to the famous 'Tank Man' photo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate creative for unintended visual or historical parallels and for sensitivity to contemporary political climates; perform contextual checks for imagery that may evoke traumatic or politically charged events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risks of rapid in-house content production
rubrics_metrics.description: PepsiCo’s in-house content arm emphasized speed and volume ('Instead of taking six months to develop an ad, we have six hours or six days'), which commentators linked to failure to properly vet the ad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance speed/cost efficiencies against the need for deliberation and external critique; rapid internal production can increase risk of tone-deaf or unvetted messaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of external agency perspective
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency will take a more balanced approach; a longer trial and error approach typically avoids controversy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use external partners or independent reviews to provide distance and candid critique that internal teams may miss due to brand immersion ('drinking the cool aid').

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt crisis response actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Pepsi® promptly removed the content, halted further rollout, and issued an apology: 'Clearly we missed the mark, and we apologize... We are removing the content and halting any further rollout.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When backlash occurs, quickly remove offending content if appropriate, halt planned distribution, and communicate remedial actions; speed of action is important to limit spread and show accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crisis communication tone and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Pepsi’s apology stated intention and remorse: 'We did not intend to make light of any serious issue. We are removing the content and halting any further rollout. We also apologize for putting Kendall Jenner in this position.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apologies should acknowledge the harm, state corrective actions taken, and avoid defensiveness; tailor messaging to affected communities and influential stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage and respond to influential stakeholders
rubrics_metrics.description: Pepsi responded to a tweet by Bernice King (Dr. Martin Luther King Jr.'s daughter) and posted apologies on its channels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor influencers, community leaders, and affected stakeholders and respond directly where appropriate; addressing high-profile critics can be important to restoring trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure and monitor brand impact metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Consumer perception scores were measured with YouGov BrandIndex’s Buzz Score and Purchase Consideration metrics showed declines: e.g., purchase consideration among millennials fell from 33% (2014) to 23% at one point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track metrics such as buzz/sentiment, purchase consideration, and other brand health indicators before and after campaigns to detect adverse impact and guide recovery strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short-term versus long-term recovery tactics
rubrics_metrics.description: Although perception recovered, purchase consideration stayed low; a limited-edition product temporarily raised numbers but they later fell back.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan both immediate remedial actions and longer-term brand recovery strategies (product initiatives, rebranding, leadership/structural changes), recognizing some effects (like purchase consideration) can persist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity and alignment with corporate mission/CSR
rubrics_metrics.description: Pepsi claimed the ad embodied their social corporate responsibility and mission statements of unity and 'Performance with Purpose,' yet critics saw a mismatch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure campaigns that touch on social issues are authentically aligned with the company’s demonstrated values and actions; inconsistent messaging invites skepticism and charges of opportunism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-release testing for unintended symbolism
rubrics_metrics.description: Viewers compared the ad imagery to real protest imagery and historical photos; lack of such checks contributed to backlash.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include image- and symbol-focused testing with diverse reviewers to flag visual metaphors that may be interpreted as co-option or trivialization of real events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakeholder/community consultation
rubrics_metrics.description: Marketing Week and commentators recommended reaching out to consumers and getting outside perspectives; the case highlights failure to 'reach out to consumers.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult relevant communities and subject-matter stakeholders (activists, community leaders) when addressing social themes; incorporate their feedback into creative decisions to avoid misrepresentation.
